mutants.description: The S_RUN window takes as its sample 'cp_sync high in any of the last BLANK_CLKS clocks' (OR of the whole blanking history) instead of the one comparator value from BLANK_CLKS clocks before high-side turn-on.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a CP excursion that happens in the last few clocks before pwm_rise but not at the tapped clock counts as a faulted cycle. fault_count_run_out reads higher and window_trip asserts after fewer real valley overcurrent cycles.

mutants.description: A TRIP_SS threshold of zero is treated as 'soft-start window trip disabled' instead of 'trip at any count'.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss programmed to 0, window_trip_SS stays low for the whole of S_SS where it should be high from the first clock of S_SS. So the supervisor completes soft start instead of going to hiccup.

after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
mutants.description: window_trip_SS is registered, so it follows the soft-start count and ss_active one clock late.
mutants.reason: When the soft-start count reaches trip_ss, window_trip_SS rises one clock late. It also stays high for one clock after S_SS is left, so a trip that coincides with SS_done is seen in S_RUN and logged by fault_cause, and the hiccup is entered a clock late.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip counts one faulted cycle too many when comparing with trip_ss, so window_trip_SS asserts when the window holds trip_ss-1 faulted cycles.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, window_trip_SS asserts and the supervisor goes to hiccup one faulted switching cycle earlier than TRIP_SS specifies. With trip_ss of 1 it trips at once with no faulted cycle.

after: always_comb window_trip    = run_active && (pmic_types_pkg::TRIP_W'(fault_count_run) + pmic_types_pkg::TRIP_W'(pwm_rise && cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1]) >= trip_run);
mutants.description: The S_RUN trip looks ahead at the sample being taken on pwm_rise, adding the entering bit without subtracting the leaving bit, instead of comparing the registered run count.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with fault_count_run at trip_run-1, a faulted sample at pwm_rise asserts window_trip one clock early. If the oldest sample leaving the window is also faulted, it raises a one-clock spurious trip that sends the supervisor to hiccup even though the count never reaches trip_run.
